subject.title: Package updater runs mutating doctor --fix without an explicit update option

question: Should ordinary `openclaw update` remain an automatic migration-and-repair transaction, or should it become non-mutating after package replacement unless the operator explicitly selects update repair?
rationale: Both choices protect a real product invariant: automatic repair helps upgrades converge, while explicit repair preserves operator approval boundaries; source inspection alone cannot choose which contract maintainers intend.

options.title: Separate update and repair
options.body: Run read-only post-upgrade checks by default and require `openclaw update repair` or another explicit opt-in before invoking `doctor --fix`.

options.title: Keep repair, disclose it
options.body: Continue automatic `doctor --fix`, but document it prominently and expose the exact planned mutations in dry-run and JSON output before confirmation.

options.title: Preserve current behavior
options.body: Treat package update authorization as including safe Doctor migrations and make only documentation or output wording changes.

recommendation.title: Separate update and repair
recommendation.body: Run read-only post-upgrade checks by default and require `openclaw update repair` or another explicit opt-in before invoking `doctor --fix`.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior appears to originate in their package post-update Doctor work, so they are best positioned to explain the migration invariant the automatic repair was intended to protect.
